I wish it didn't, as the big bulky S3 Frontier looks best to me with a similarly big band. It doesn't taper enough for me to really care, but in a perfect world it wouldn't at all. Overall this is a great and reasonably priced pair of bands that allow your Gear watch to pull off some fresh new looks.

To add insult to injury, Buy-Batteries won't replace my case and Amazon won't support me either. They claim that there's a 30-day warranty and since I'm past it there's nothing that can be done. I pointed out that the defect didn't start to happen until after the 30-day period and a phone case should last longer than 6 months, right? I also pointed out that the case failed through no fault of mine and it's obviously defective and should be replaced. Logic doesn't work. So, buyer beware - Buy-Batteries is shady, and Amazon doesn't take responsibility for their sellers. Buy directly from Speck if you want a Candyshell case - it's more expensive but well worth it.

text: I love the original Easy View mount, so when I upgraded to a much larger phone (Nexus 6) that wouldn't fit in that mount, I went looking for another iOttie that could accommodate the behemoth. That led me to try the Easy View 2. With a normal-sized phone, the Easy View 2 can be operated single-handedly. Just slide the right edge of your phone in, pushing against the right-side grip so that it slides out enough to hold your phone. Springs in the slide mechanism allow it to maintain a tight (but not too tight) grip on the phone. When you use a larger phone, like my Nexus 6, you'll also need to slide the left-side grip out. That makes it a two-handed operation. I would prefer that it be one-handed, but it's not that bad. The grip part attaches to the stand with the same sized ball head that the original Easy View uses. I swapped out the stands, because the one that comes with this model is a little too short; it doesn't allow me to rotate my phone in landscape orientation without bumping the instrument panel. It also causes the phone's charging cable to bend right below the plug, as it presses against the dashboard. I prefer the taller stand that came with the original Easy View, as it gives me a little more clearance.

text: After recently loosing my Apple watch on a trail while mountain biking because of a sheared-off strap, I came to Amazon looking for the most rugged sports-oriented band I could find. I was immediately attracted to this one, and when I received it I was initially pleased with its comfort, ease of use, and apparent high-quality workmanship and construction. I've since returned it. As others here have written, the small spring pins that hold the nylon band to the aluminum end pieces that mate with the watch are indeed the fatal flaw. After my watch fell off for the THIRD time - and each occurrence was in the midst of normal, low-stress household activities - I decided I was done. It's a shame, because I love the band otherwise. I think the spring pins they use are pretty standard for metal watch bands, but I suspect the mechanism at work here is that the nylon catches much more easily on the collar sleeve of the pin, pulling IT back and releasing it, whereas in a metal band the pin would be sitting in a smooth metal bore with no small fibers to pull on it. In other words, I don't think the pins themselves are garbage per se, but rather the problem is how they're being used. The manufacturer either needs to ditch the pins entirely or somehow address the fact that they release at inopportune times. Were it not for this serious issue, I'd happily give it a five star rating.

text: SNATCH is the much anticipated "sequel" to director Guy Ritchie's hugely successful affair, LOCK, STOCK & TWO SMOKING BARRELS. But where the first film was fresh and original, the second seems to be more a blank copy, which is forced to exaggerate typical "crowd-pleasures" such as violence and "hip" filmmaking. SNATCH manages to create several funny moments, for sure, but for the most part the film loses itself in its own ego (it's as if Guy Ritchie is saying "we're the coolest people around"). It's just a little too much of everything in SNATCH. But maybe I'm judging it a bit too harsh. Let's focus on the positive things... The cast is great. Brad Pitt is funny as the Irish Gypsy, One Punch' Mickey O'Neil. Dennis Farina is always good as a gangster. Benicio Del Toro has way too little screen-time. And Vinnie Jones fits the role as a tough torpedo. And there are several memorable moments and quotes in the film (Uncle Avi (talking to Bullet-Tooth Tony): "What should I call you? Bullet? Tony?" / Bullet-Tooth Tony: "You can call me Susan if it makes you happy"). But I guess the point that I'm trying to get across is this: The film may deserve more credit than what I'm giving it, but because of its excellent predecessor, I couldn't help but feel all the more disappointed about this one (million dollars may be a lot of money, but not compared to a billion dollars).

text: After switching jobs I had to switch mobile carriers from Verizon to ATT. I work primarily out of a basement home office that is below grade and poured concrete walls. For whatever reason my coverage with ATT was non-existent in my home office with frequent dropped calls. Mobile coverage is routinely 3 bars elsewhere in home. As my mobile phone is my main work phone line, I needed a reliable solution. After much research, I decided that the Wilson Electronics 815226 Cell Phone Signal Cradle Booster might be a reasonable solution. After plugging in the cradle booster and situating the magnet mount antenna my mobile reception went from 1-2 bars (at best) to routinely achieving 4 bars. The main downside to this system is that the phone needs to be in the cradle at all times. However, as I have it mounted on my work desk I simply use a blue tooth headset or the phone on speaker and it has worked very reliably. Occasionally still will drop a call when in the cradle, but a huge improvement over no reception and/or constantly dropping calls. One potentially useful tip is that I have the mini-magnet antenna mounted on a the bottom of a metal coffee can that I then placed bottom side up on a book shelf closest to where the mobile signal is best in the room. Not the most attractive arrangement, but since my home office is not in a public area it is fine. Overall, very happy with this purchase.

This causes too much vibration to be recorded when using the cam as a dash cam, bike cam, etc. Although the unit has a steady mode, the amplitude of of movement conveyed by the plastic mounts is beyond the ability to stabilize the picture electronically. The water tight housing is effective yet heavy, further exaggerating the camera's movement like a lollipop on a flimsy stick. Like every action-cam I've experienced, at any price level, the lens creates severe barrel distortion. I suspect this is because more elements would increase size, weight, and cost. The price, addition of anti shake and a view screen are all improvements over the far more expensive GoPro. There is no option for a remote, slow motion, or remote viewing via smart phone or tablet. Although these features are not expected for the price, there is no upgrade path. The sj1000 is a great option for adding multiple cameras to a shoot. I could buy five of these for less than one top of line GoPro.

text: I like to leave chargers wherever I can, so I don't have to worry about dead batteries. It's a little trickier with dedicated chargers like the Apple watch - most people don't have 5 or six cables lying around, like with lightning, USB Micro, USB-C, etc. This is a nice piece that I can just stick in my laptop bag, and not have to worry about packing a watch cable as long as I have my bag. It is relatively small, and nice that it works well with USB-A and USB-C. The issues though, are these. The rigid design gives you a nice compact package, but at the expense of flexibility. It's great to plug into the side of a laptop, but any USB port that isn't horizontal, and you're out of luck. Or even if it's horizontal, but without a good way to support the watch, again, out of luck (it does work somewhat, but don't want to put that kind of stress on the USB port). It's much easier to just have a cable that can be plugged in anywhere. The flexibility of space/orientation and much more valuable than the USB-A vs. USB-C choice. Maybe if this was cheaper it would be great, but at $20, it should be better than a cable, not worse. It works just fine, so not going below three stars, but I would not buy again, or recommend it.

Also when you dip the film in the solution, you don't want it to be dripping wet but you also don't want it to not be wet enough, otherwise it'll stick immediately to the watch face before you have time to align it, making it hard to pull off. On film 4 I finally got it!

The old suction based system’s I have used in the past routinely dropped my phone on the floor, just when I needed it to be in place… The system that holds the base unit onto the magnet is simple, adjustable, and appears bombproof. My kit came with a small white envelope containing a pad with a very strong solvent that is used to clean the dashboard prior to sticking the base of the unit in place. text: I bought this from a company that had the product listed as "Fulfilled by Amazon," and they quickly resolved my problems, less than two hours after I voiced my concerns. This review is just a warning to anyone who might have the same issues. The battery I bought here is counterfeit. I suspected something was wrong when the battery charge got significantly worse after a few weeks, and I looked up how to identify fake Samsung batteries online. The easiest way to tell if it is fake is to peel the label back, since counterfeiters have figured out how to make the outside appearance look identical to genuine batteries. Also, different genuine batteries of the same model will have differences in the labels, so you can't depend on the printed label alone. The battery I received has two obvious hallmarks of counterfeit batteries, and a few others I won't describe here. First, the other side of the sticker label is shiny. Genuine Samsung batteries have the same dull grey color on both sides. Second, and most obvious, is that there is no NFC capability on this battery, and after peeling the label back, it is obviously missing the NFC antenna. If you are suspicious about your battery, there are guides on Youtube to show you how to figure out if you have a fake or genuine battery. I would not at all be surprised that any battery under $10 is counterfeit, and much lower quality than a genuine battery. Overall I would not recommend buying a Samsung battery from anyone but a very trusted seller who guarantees genuine products. You might think, "Oh who cares if it is counterfeit as long as it works," but you'll end up wasting time and money dealing with crappy counterfeits if you aren't careful.

text: This product, in and of itself, is fantastic. It does everything it's trying to do, and does it well. Specifically, the construction is superb. The swivel action is perfect, as well. It feels like it will last forever. There are 2 major concerns with this product, though. First of all, and I think most importantly, you have to understand that you'll be putting your very sensitive piece of extremely expensive tech hardware directly in front of a thing that blows incredibly hot air out. Most cars are pushing out 140 degree air to heat the car up. This is not good for your phone, and since the magnets are metallic, it turns your phone into a burning hot mess. You'll have to either close off the vent the phone is attached to, or not use the dashboard heat at all, and only use the floorboard and defrost vents, or you'll risk the phone's lifespan by constantly overheating it. Second of all, my car has horizontally oriented vents. Within one single use of this mount, the vent that the phone is attached to is now unable to stay in the "up" position, and reverts immediately to the "down" position, even if the mount is removed. The weight of the mount and the phone completely removed the vent's ability to hold anything other than the totally "down" position. So, if you completely understand the 2 big negatives, and are fine with them, then this product is perfect.

text: Headline says it all. Really, really a waste of time. Couldn't even beat another garbage adapter I bought here on Amazon - Electop ASIN B07B47V967 - also claiming 5Ggps speeds. This one barely managed low 30's MBps vs mid 40's MBps for the Electop. Note the difference in units: ?bps vs ?Bps. Typically data communication transfer speeds are expressed in bps (bits per second) & data storage transfer speeds are expressed in Bps (Bytes per second). As there are 8 bits per byte, the conversion from one to the other is either 8 bits times or 8 bits divided. In this case, 5Gbps (Giga bits per second) is 625MBps. So ... neither this adapter or the Electop come even close to that theoretical limit. On the other hand, a UGREEN (ASIN B079K773M7) adapter also bought here on Amazon does yield speeds comparable to those tested using the device directly plugged into a USB C port on another PC. So it's NOT an issue with the PC I'm using, which by the way has two (2) USB SS (Super Speed - rated at 5Gbps) ports. Not only are the speed claims bogus but the device's USB A connector isn't designed properly. It can be over inserted into a USB A port which results in a disconnection. In other words, inserted past a certain point the device disconnects so what was originally seen/recognized by file explorer (or its equivalent) 'disappears'.

Once in the car, touch one button to turn on the power and then a second to turn on the FM transmission capability and from there, you are all set. Touch the play button on the front of the device and your phone's media player is automatically engaged, and you can skip forward and back between songs by touching the buttons on each side. As a St. Louis Cardinals fan living in South Carolina, I cannot get radio broadcasts over the air but with the T505 and the MLB app, I can listen to every game live, whether in my car or over my home stereo. One limitation to FM transmitters is that there is sometimes a need to find a new frequency because of static caused by nearby radio stations, but that is handled very easily by the T505; touch the button on the back and the nice British sounding lady will happily instruct you to tune your radio to a new frequency she has searched out for you.

text: So I tested this on my iPhone SE 2020. If you are using charging peripherals however, because how these phones aren't really designed with a ring of magnets interfering with the charging coil, it runs much hotter (which is bad for your battery) and sometimes can have problems charging with either a normal wireless charger, the OEM Apple Magsafe charger, or a 3rd party magnetic charger. Charging performance however is still better than taping a magsafe ring to your existing case, but I do wish this case used a more protective design. text: A car mount with wireless charging for $25 is a good value and if that's all this charger were supposed to do, I'd be happier. It's the "remaining closed" function I've found wanting and I've see several other reviews mentioning random opening/closing - usually at just the right time for the phone to fly across the car or burrow itself into the seat/center console gap. HOWEVER, I think I've figured this out. I noticed my phone (Samsung S9) wasn't charging reliably while sitting in the mount so I adjusted the "foot" of the mount down to better align the charging receiver on the phone with the charging transmitter on the mount. Since I did that, the charger remains closed once the phone is placed on it. It seems it's not just a simple open/close function with the open portion activate by putting your finger on the sensor. It seems the mount is looking to confirm charging is actually happening to keep the motorized arms closed. Hope this solves some other folks' issues with this product.

text: I have used these types of overlays many times on phones, PDA's, etc. By taking a few simple steps, the process goes smoothly and you get good results. First, The tiny little cleaning cloth that comes with the protector is too small. It's nice that they give you one, but it's easier if you use a big one. I have several of these lying around - they are included when you buy better sunglasses, binoculars or other optics. They give them away at eyeglass shops and camera stores. Get the screen very clean. Next, put on either cotton or latex gloves so you don't smudge the protector as you're putting it on. When applying the protector, be patient. I found it easiest to line it up on the bottom of the screen and gently lay it down. It didn't line up perfectly the first time, but using a plastic ball point pen cap or similar item, you can lift it back off and try again. It may take a few tries to lay it down perfectly aligned. Finally, working from the center using the cleaning cloth, work out the air bubbles. I have never been able to get every single bubble out, but I only see them when the phone is off. When it's illuminated, they are pretty much invisible. Even though this is supposed to be re-usable, what's the point? I keep it clean using the lens cloth until it gets to scratched up or stops sticking down to the screen. At that point, throw it out and get a new one. The last one I had lasted well over a year.

text: I bought this for an HTC Inspire, though the packaging indicated HTC Desire -- same phone body, or so I hear. I had wanted a case immediately and it did the job, but I got tired of the girly purple. So I gave this case a try. This case was literally one fourth the price of the one from Best Buy, yet the difference in quality between the name brand and this likely "knock off" is negligible. Both appear to be made of the same smooth, rubber-like material; both are about the same thickness; both fit the phone snugly. There is one place, on the front top (earpiece) area, where the expensive case was slightly more customized to the opening. However, on the reverse side, the holes for the camera lens and flash were incredibly precise on this case, whereas they weren't on the much more expensive case from Best Buy. In terms of looks, this case is more professional and mature looking...it is a smoky clear case with subtle circle patterns. The phone color and logo show through, but there is some tint. As far as I can tell, it offers the same basic level of protection as the rubber skin case I replaced. Bottom line: At less than $5, it is a great deal. You will pay two, three, or four times as much at a retail store.

text: Short version: yes, I recommend this watchband, but with caveats depending upon use and user... The band is thinner and more flexible than the smooth Apple Sport band, thanks to the "ridged" pattern of the band. This also means that the band will stretch more if pulled or caught on something. The primary difference is how it buckles. With the Apple Sport band, the strap is pushed onto a round stud and the loose strap inserted through a slot and trapped between band and wrist. This strap requires threading through first one loop, then the other, and sliding it while pushing the strap down onto a rectangular stud. This may be more secure, or it may be needed due to the additional flexibility of the band. For active people, who need a strong band or may get it caught on things, the original band is stronger. For normal wear, this band should be good, aside from the extra step buckling it on.
title: More flexible than Apple Sport band. Buckles a bit differently.

text: This phone is peppy, has a great screen, good call quality, good signal reception ... no complaints at all in these areas. My only complaint is that the phone tends to hold a shape. I've had two of these, and they seem to change shape almost on a daily basis (which corner is lowest relative to the other corners). My theory is that the metal trim (a thin plate) on the back of the phone prevents the rest of the phone from returning to its original shape after the phone is stressed. Also, sometimes the metal trim on the back develops wrinkles or lines. I have no concerns about safety or ruggedness. When the first one of these I owned began to shape shift, I destructively tested it to see how tough it was. I couldn't cause any sort of failure by dropping it from shoulder height onto a tile floor. I also couldn't twist it too far out of shape by hand, and when I tried to buckle it by putting the center of the phone on the edge of a stair and applying force at the ends, I could not buckle it using a large fraction of my body weight. Although bent, the screen worked up until I cracked it after several tries. I have a plastic Samsung J3 (a cheaper phone), and it always has the same shape. A phone that changes shape when not damaged is annoying. It makes it harder to evaluate damage (and with anything containing a lithium battery, I will discard it if I even suspect it is damaged). Motorola/Lenovo -- Lose the metal from the design. Plastic phones are fine.

The end that connects to your device is the MALE end (plugs into whatever you are charging). IF your charging cable ends in USB-C, then order this with FEMALE USB-C end, and MALE Micro-USB end. text: Marketed as a super long selfie stick for camera phones, it definitely delivers on that account. But marketing aside, this is essentially a tripod that is light enough to utilize as a selfie-stick and/or monopod... The portion that the photographer holds is merely the folded tripod legs with no special design for better grip nor to mount the included but separate camera shutter bluetooth remote. It is most useful as a versatile travel tripod, monopod and/or selfie-stick for phone/GoPro cameras. $20 price puts it right in the middle of the pricing spectrum for this kind of product, representing a good value. Here are the product pluses: + infinitely adjustable length between 20” to a very long 67.3” + weighs in at a light 16.6 oz (18.6 oz with phone mount attached) + combination of stiffness+lightness is easy to control even fully extended to 67 inches + includes Bluetooth remote shutter trigger (both Android and iOS support) + ¼” screw mount for included phone/tablet and GoPro mounting plates (although can only handle tablet up to 8”) Here are the product minuses: - tripod legs are a bit uncomfortable to hold as a selfie stick, especially for smaller hands - the feature of 67” extension also means that the smallest length is 20” which is not as compact for travel as other sticks and a bit tall to use as a tabletop tripod. - no built-in holder for separate bluetooth remote requires 2 hand operation and easy to misplace - build quality is very good for light aluminum gauge, certainly adequate for phones and GoPros but a mirrorless camera or DSLR would be too much weight to handle with precise control. - not designed to be submerged in water

However, the magnets in the official magsafe charger are too weak to reliably hold onto your phone in a car during bumpy road conditions. While a regular 6" iphone 12/13 attaches to the magsafe charger fine, it slides off fairly easily when you pull on it. The larger/heavier 6.7" max/plus iphones will definitely slip off way too easily. Even a small bump is probably enough to knock either of these phones off. I already have another magnetic car phone mount that has MUCH stronger magnets, and will just continue to use that and plug my iphone in separately. This type of magsafe holder may work fine for a desk mount/holder, but not for a car. I do not recommend anyone get this product

Secondly, there is a fairly large space between the port opening in the bumper, and the actual device. For example, the sound mute switch is really deep, making it hard to reach. From a manufacturing perspective, I probably would have sunk the bezel more around each of the ports. Thirdly, the bezel around the power port (in the bottom middle of the case), is pretty sharp. I saw another reviewer who mentioned this, and thought perhaps it was an over exaggeration, but it was true. The bezel around the headphone jack is actually pretty great. If they had done the same around all the other ports, I probably would have added another star. It wasn't a completely horrible product, but it wasn't really what I was looking for in terms of slim protection for my phone. I've actually seen quite a few other cases that are made much more horribly than this. It's really not bad. You have to decide for yourself, how much you like bumper cases, and whether or not you will like this one. If you're on the fence, I'd check out something else.

I am giving the protector 4 rather than 5 because the cutouts at the top are not perfect. The two little circles and home key are, but the long one at the top for the speaker is longer than it needs to be and off center. The speaker is not covered, but it is at the side of the cut out rather than in the center. Yes, I know this is a nit that I am picking, but that is why I am giving it a 4.
title: 5 Stars, Except Microphone Cutout Not Quite Perfect

label: Neutral
text: Haven't had to use it too much, but seems ok. It does take a bit of lung capacity to really get anything out of the little one's nose with this thing (His mom can't manage), and it doesn't seem any better at the hard burgers than the regular bulb syringe. However, we recently used it for a runny nose when the bulb syringe didn't work, and it sure seemed to get a lot more snot out. Good product, a little gross to think about at first, a little hard to suck through, but I will definitely keep using it and am glad I bought it.
title: Good for runny, not for crusty. A little hard to suck through.
